Q: SVG animation works in Chrome but not in Firefox: the airplane doesn't move A:

The main reason this animation doesn't work in Firefox is that the browser interprets the animateMotion element much more strictly than Chrome in terms of the coordinate system and target selectors.To resolve the issue, you need to move the animateMotion block from outside the #circle group you want to animate and place it directly inside that group; this way, the xlink:href=“#circle” reference is no longer needed, and Firefox can find the target much more easily. Additionally, to prevent coordinate shifts in Firefox, keeping the plane's starting coordinates close to the (0,0) point and using only href instead of xlink:href, which is the modern standard, will completely eliminate compatibility issues.This minor structural change will ensure that the plane follows the same path in both Chrome and Firefox

Q: why does buildozer crash on ubuntu 24.04 while running buildozer -v android debug A:

The preadv error is a hard conflict between the NDK and outdated C-code in that dev-branch. To fix this, you must switch to a stable setup and flush your caches.

  1. Delete the .buildozer folder in your project (crucial to remove broken C-caches).

  2. Update your .spec to this verified configuration for KivyMD 2.x:

Ini, TOML

requirements = python3,kivy==2.3.1,https://github.com/kivymd/KivyMD/archive/master.zip,materialyoucolor,asynckivy,asyncgui android.api = 33 android.minapi = 24 
android.ndk = 25b 
android.archs = arm64-v8a android.enable_androidx = True

This specific combination of NDK 25b and the master branch avoids the preadv link errors. If it still crashes, ensure you are using JDK 17 in your environment, as it's required for newer Gradle versions used with API 33.

Q: Python Polars Read Zipped CSV A:

IMO one useful approach for zipfiles that I haven't seen discussed in detail is to learn about fsspec url-chaining.

The example below works far quicker than any of the other more explicit attempts I've made to open the zip file. It's particularly good for online datasets

import polars as pl
df = pl.read_csv("zip://path/to/csv.csv::https://www.my_data.com/downloads/zipped_dataset",infer_schema=False)
